title.narrative: ASEAN-Australia One Health Training and Capacity Building Investment

description.narrative: This investment builds regional capacity to prevent and respond to emerging infectious diseases. It uses a One Health approach to reduce the risk of pandemics from zoonotic disease outbreaks, including through the ASEAN-Australia One Health Fellowship program.

description.narrative: The ASEAN-Australia One Health Training and Capacity Building Investment contributed to strengthening regional architecture in ASEAN through the development and adoption of regional strategies, frameworks and roadmaps. Australia’s support for developing and implementing the ASEAN Leaders’ Declaration on One Health Initiatives through the ASEAN One Health Joint Plan of Action (2023-2030), ASEAN One Health Fellowships, and ASEAN One Health Network was acknowledged in the Chairman’s Statement of the 2025 ASEAN Post-Ministerial Conference 10+1 Session.

The ASEAN-Australia One Health Training and Capacity Building Investment contributed to strengthening regional architecture in ASEAN through the development and adoption of regional strategies, frameworks and roadmaps. ‍ Australia provided funding for the development of the ASEAN Leaders’ Declaration on One Health Initiative, adopted at the 42nd ASEAN Summit in May 2023, and the implementation of the Declaration through the development of the TOR of the One Health Network and the Joint Action Plan on One Health. In the Chairman’s Statement of the 3rd ASEAN-Australia Summit in September 2023, Australia’s support for the development and implementation of the Declaration was appreciated.

The ASEAN-Australia One Health Training and Capacity Building Investment is helping improve health services through the provision of training and professional development programs, and strengthening policy and regulatory frameworks, to align with international health standards. ‍ Australia provided funding for the ASEAN-Australia One Health Fellowship Program, which offered 45 fellowships to One Health professionals from a range of fields. These fellowships included studying an online Graduate Certificate in One Health, attendance at research training workshops and participation in the ASEAN-Australia One Health Community of Practice. ‍ Australia provided funding to support the development and implementation of the ASEAN Leaders’ Declaration on One Health Initiative. The Declaration and its two implementation mechanisms support the One Health Joint Plan of Action (2022-2026) and aims to improve regional and national capabilities to strengthen health systems and develop multisectoral collaboration and coordination of One Health initiatives.

The ASEAN-Australia One Health Training and Capacity Building Investment is helping improve health services through training and professional development programs, and strengthening policy and regulatory frameworks to align with international health standards. This Investment promotes a One Health approach, recognising the interconnectedness of people, animal and environmental health. ‍ In the reporting period, Australia funded the ASEAN-Australia One Health Fellowship Program, which supported 45 ASEAN officials and academics to improve technical capacity across human, animal and environmental health. Fellows are expected to apply their training to be able to better address specific zoonotic risk factors in our region. ‍ Australia also supported the development and implementation of the 2023 ASEAN Leaders’ Declaration on One Health Initiative and the One Health Joint Plan of Action (2022-2026). This aims to improve regional and national capabilities to strengthen health systems, and help develop multisectoral collaboration and coordination of One Health initiatives.

The ASEAN-Australia One Health Training and Capacity Building Investment is helping strengthen workforce skills and capacity for management of infectious diseases, including One Health skills and practice in general workforces and strengthened One Health workforces. ‍ Australia provided funding for the ASEAN-Australia One Health Fellowship Program, which offered 45 fellowships to One Health professionals from a range of fields. These fellowships included studying an online Graduate Certificate in One Health, attendance at research training workshops and participation in the ASEAN-Australia One Health Community of Practice, with the purpose of improving technical health capacity through the One Health approach. ‍
Australia provided funding for the annual in-person workshop held in Indonesia, facilitated by Murdoch University. It gave fellows the opportunity to network, engage in project discussions, and establish collaborative relationships within the ASEAN-Australia One Health Community of Practice.
